events.title: The Teutonic Knights defeat a Lithuanian army at Rudau
events.description: Near Rudau in Sambia, the Teutonic Knights under Grand Master Winrich von Kniprode defeated a Lithuanian army led by Grand Duke Algirdas and his brother Kęstutis, which had invaded Prussia. It was one of the Order's most celebrated successes against Lithuania.

events.title: Musa Çelebi becomes ruler of Ottoman Thrace as Süleyman is killed
events.description: During the Ottoman Interregnum, Süleyman, a son of Bayezid I, was captured and strangled after his army defected to his brother Musa Çelebi at Edirne. Musa became ruler of the Ottoman dominions in Thrace.

events.title: The Lancastrian army wins at St Albans and frees Henry VI
events.description: In the second battle fought at St Albans, Hertfordshire, the Lancastrian army defeated the Yorkist army and released King Henry VI from captivity. The Wars of the Roses were fought between the houses of York and Lancaster for the English throne.

events.title: Giordano Bruno is burned at the stake in Rome
events.description: Condemned by the Inquisition for heresy, the Dominican philosopher was burned in the Campo de' Fiori. His views included an infinite universe with countless worlds; a statue of him now stands there.
events.html: Condemned by the Inquisition for heresy, the Dominican philosopher was burned in the Campo de' Fiori. His views included an infinite universe with countless worlds; a statue of him now stands there.

events.title: An earthquake and megatsunami strike Ambon Island
events.description: An earthquake in the Maluku Islands raised a tsunami up to 100 metres high on Ambon Island, killing over 2,000 people. It was the first detailed documentation of a tsunami in Indonesia and the largest recorded there; a submarine landslide was likely the cause.

events.title: House elects Thomas Jefferson President after an electoral tie
events.description: On the 36th ballot, the House of Representatives broke the tie between Jefferson and his running mate Aaron Burr. The crisis led to the Twelfth Amendment, separating votes for President and Vice-President.

events.title: Committee that became the Red Cross meets in Geneva
events.description: Five Genevans, including Henri Dunant, founded a committee to aid wounded soldiers, inspired by Dunant's account of Solferino. It became the International Committee of the Red Cross.
events.html: Five Genevans, including Henri Dunant, founded a committee to aid wounded soldiers, inspired by Dunant's account of Solferino. It became the International Committee of the Red Cross.

events.title: H. L. Hunley sinks USS Housatonic
events.description: The Confederate submarine rammed a torpedo into the Union warship off Charleston, the first sinking of an enemy ship by a submarine. The Hunley was lost with all eight crew that night.
events.html: The Confederate submarine rammed a torpedo into the Union warship off Charleston, the first sinking of an enemy ship by a submarine. The Hunley was lost with all eight crew that night.

events.title: First issue of News-Week is published
events.description: The weekly news magazine, later Newsweek, was launched in New York as a rival to Time. It became one of the leading American news weeklies of the 20th century.

events.title: China invades Vietnam
events.description: Chinese troops crossed Vietnam's northern border to punish Hanoi for invading Cambodia. Both sides claimed victory after a month of fighting that cost tens of thousands of lives.

song: Folk singers of northern England (Yorkshire and Northumbria)
An old English folk song in which a singer asks a lost love to do impossible tasks. It is sung to a tune collected from a lead miner in 1947.
